summary: Procurement source-to-pay domain foundation adds supplier qualification, purchase requisition approval, purchase order issuance, three-way match metadata, and SAP MM/SRM parity-map linkage while explicitly refusing durable persistence, supplier-network calls, Workflow execution, inventory mutation, payment execution, cloud deployment, and runtime audit-chain claims.

findings: The implementation is a small pure-domain state/evidence model, not a monolithic ERP or supplier portal clone.
Validation is explicit and guard-clause based with no hidden side effects.
Flat procurement microservice destination improves SAP MM/SRM parity without creating microservices/erp.
Capability flags and evidence rows keep cloud/runtime claims honest until adapters land.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if unqualified suppliers, unapproved requisitions, unissued POs, quantity mismatches, amount mismatches, unsafe refs, credential-shaped evidence refs, or malformed currency values are accepted.
findings: Positive source-to-pay flow and negative guard rails are covered.
Types map directly to supplier qualification, requisition, PO, and three-way match concepts common to source-to-pay systems.
Focused procurement tests/clippy, ERP parity map tests/clippy, 26-package enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, data_class scan, and quality-marker scan passed.

F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A flat domain foundation gives ERP parity a service-owned first write path while keeping supplier networks, storage, payment, Workflow, and cloud adapters out of scope.
rejected_reasons: Marketplace-only composition left SAP MM/SRM procurement without a bounded service owner.
Supplier portal/network runtime requires authentication, external delivery channels, and durable storage beyond this slice.

findings: No credentials, external network calls, payment rails, or supplier portal integration are introduced.
Source and audit refs reject traversal, whitespace/control, and credential-shaped strings.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Pure string/enum/money validation only; no I/O or unbounded data access exists.

findings.summary: No database, network, filesystem, or hot runtime path is introduced.

data_class_touched: FINANCIAL amount and matched quantity metadata
findings: SAP/Oracle/Coupa official materials inform source-to-pay coverage only; no exhaustive vendor parity or proprietary behavior clone is claimed.
The change is additive: one new crate/spec/catalog row and parity-map references; no migration or external resource is introduced.
Static evidence, task rows, and audit-chain rows document the change; runtime audit emission remains a non-claim.
No production user or data migration exists.
Package name follows oya-procurement-source-to-pay-domain and flat microservice layout.
Machine-readable procurement spec and existing task ledger capture the slice without creating root markdown sprawl.
New code is isolated to microservices/procurement plus Enterprise Suite parity map references.
Clean architecture is preserved: domain crate depends only on data boundary kernel and std.
No new third-party dependencies were added; Cargo.lock changed only for the new workspace package.
specs/microservices/procurement.json parses successfully and evidence follows prior multispectrum shape.
Three-way match is deterministic exact quantity/amount validation with no tolerance or hidden state.

M1_challenge_assumption.finding: Challenged whether procurement should be folded into marketplace; creating a separate source-to-pay domain is more aligned with ERP MM/SRM parity and future cloud integration.

M2_zoomed_out_fit.finding: Complements HR/payroll/accounting foundations and improves ERP parity while keeping no microservices/erp monolith.
